newsitem.title: USA: US cash hog prices may reach $60 by summer - Refco.
newsitem.headline: US cash hog prices may reach $60 by summer - Refco.

text.p: U.S. cash hog prices should rally to the mid $50s per cwt by summer and may even reach the high $50s or $60 if U.S. exports grow following Taiwan's pork export ban, Refco Global Research analyst Jack Weaver said.

But the rise should prove short lived with a drop to the mid $40s expected by fall and potentially even low $40s (for Iowa interior hogs) amid expanding hog numbers, Weaver said in remarks prepared for a series of outlook seminars this week.
"The expected increase in hog numbers comes from attractive margins from late spring 1996 through early 1997," Weaver said.
"Sow slaughter dropped significantly from mid-1996 on, lending support to ideas of expansion," he noted.
Weaver said pork production has shown year-on-year declines for seven consecutive quarters but the series should be broken this year with the potential for significant gains by fall.
He also noted hog weights so far in 1997 had been two to three lbs over a year earlier.
"This gain is expected to continue due to lower feed costs and will add one percent or more to pork production in 1997," he said.

Weaver forecast cattle prices in Texas would average $65.00 to $66.00 per cwt during 1997 with seasonal studies implying the high has just been made or will be made within the next few weeks in the $68 to $72 range.
He said domestic beef demand may be lackluster by mid-1997.
"Retail prices are close to lows made in 1996 but retail margins have deteriorated to where prices will turn higher into early summer," Weaver said.
